card.title: Conservation of momentum
card.says: when the **net external force** on a system is zero ($\sum\vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0}$), the system's total momentum stays constant—even in inelastic collisions where kinetic energy is lost to heat or deformation.
card.from: Newton's third law combined with impulse: during a collision, objects 1 and 2 exert equal and opposite forces ($\vec{F}_{12} = -\vec{F}_{21}$) for the same contact time $\Delta t$, so their impulses cancel ($\Delta\vec{p}_1 + \Delta\vec{p}_2 = \vec{0}$).
card.useWhen: two or more objects collide, stick together, or push off each other (recoil or explosion) on a frictionless surface or during a brief impact where external forces are negligible.
card.example: A $2\text{ kg}$ cart at $+6\text{ m/s}$ collides and sticks to a stationary $4\text{ kg}$ cart: $2(6) + 4(0) = (2 + 4)v \Rightarrow 12 = 6v \Rightarrow v = +2\text{ m/s}$.
card.analogy: Standing on ice skates and throwing a heavy ball forward pushes you backward with equal and opposite momentum—the pair's combined momentum stays zero.
